title: tracing: ctf: validate socket address length and family
body:
The CTF tracing hooks for socket operations were previously casting `msg_name` or `addr` pointers to `struct sockaddr` and accessing the `sa_family` member without verifying if the provided address length was sufficient. This could lead to out-of-bounds memory reads or kernel panics if a NULL pointer or an insufficient length was provided by the caller.

This commit adds defensive checks to:
1. Verify pointers are non-NULL before dereferencing.
2. Ensure the provided address length is at least the size of `struct net_sockaddr` before reading the address family.
3. Validate that the buffer is large enough for the specific family (AF_INET vs AF_INET6) before calling net_addr_ntop.
4. Correctly handle IPv6 address and port tracing, which was previously missing or handled as IPv4.

title: boards: shields: rk055hdmipi4ma0: enable and fix LVGL demos on mimxrt700_evk
body:
Fixes #104692 

## What the change does
Renames `sram1` (`0x20200000`, 2MB) to `LVGL_BUF` in the board overlay so `CONFIG_LV_Z_VDB_CUSTOM_SECTION=y` (already in `.conf`) maps LVGL VDBs to fast internal SRAM. Sets `LV_Z_VDB_SIZE=20` and disables `LV_Z_FULL_REFRESH` for `mimxrt700_evk` only. All other boards using this shield are unaffected.

## Why this approach
`sram1` is explicitly designated for non-cacheable NPU/GPU/Display data in `nxp_rt7xx_common.dtsi` — the correct location for LVGL VDBs. At 20% VDB size, two buffers = ~820KB, fits in the 2MB `sram1` bank. The previous default (full-frame VDB) required ~4MB, overflowing internal SRAM entirely.

## Assumptions
- `sram1` has no other consumers on `mimxrt700_evk` CM33 CPU0 — confirmed by checking `mimxrt700_evk_mimxrt798s_cm33_cpu0.dts` (`zephyr,sram` points to `sram0`).

body:
## Summary

Add the `rtc@40044000` device tree node to `r7fa4m2ax.dtsi`, enabling hardware RTC support for the Renesas RA4M2 series.

## Problem

The RA4M2 SoC has a built-in RTC hardware block at address `0x40044000`, widely used in embedded applications. However, the Zephyr device tree for RA4M2 did not include this RTC node, making it impossible to use the existing `rtc_renesas_ra` driver on RA4M2.

## Solution

Add the RTC device tree node with:
- **Address**: `0x40044000`, size `0x80`
- **Clock source**: SUBLCK (32768 Hz)
- **Interrupts**: IRQ 4 (carry), IRQ 5 (periodic), IRQ 6 (alarm)
- **Status**: `disabled` by default

## Testing

The patch was tested on a `ra_eco_ra4m2` board. The device was successfully initialized:

```

RTC: time set to 2026-01-01 00:00:00
```

Build output:
- FLASH: 57440 B (10.96%)
- RAM: 9288 B (7.09%)

- [x] Device tree change only
- [x] Follows existing RA4 series DTSI conventions (see `r7fa4l1bx.dtsi`)

title: Bluetooth: Host: Fix AoD 2US CTE type validation in conn CTE TX params
labels: area: Bluetooth;area: Tests;area: Bluetooth Host;backport v4.4-branch
body:
The host's `valid_conn_cte_tx_params()` in `direction.c` has a
copy-paste bug where `BT_DF_CTE_TYPE_AOD_1US` is checked twice
instead of checking `BT_DF_CTE_TYPE_AOD_1US` and
`BT_DF_CTE_TYPE_AOD_2US`:

```c
if ((params->cte_types & BT_DF_CTE_TYPE_AOD_1US ||
     params->cte_types & BT_DF_CTE_TYPE_AOD_1US) &&
```
This means when only AoD 2US is requested, the host skips antenna
ID validation before forwarding parameters to the controller.

The controller (`ll_df_set_conn_cte_tx_params` in `ull_df.c`)
correctly validates both AoD 1US and 2US, so in practice the
controller rejects invalid parameters regardless. 

Regarding the tests: the existing test suite sends HCI commands
directly to the controller, bypassing the host validation layer.
This means the new tests pass regardless of the host fix. They
do not directly verify the host bug. Their value is regression
coverage for AoD 2US in isolation at the controller level: the
existing `too_long`/`too_short` tests only exercise the combined
AOA|AOD_1US|AOD_2US case, so a regression specific to 2US-only
handling in the controller would previously go undetected.

Testing the host validation layer directly would require either
calling `bt_df_set_conn_cte_tx_param()` through the host API
(needing a `bt_conn` in connected state) or exposing
`valid_conn_cte_tx_params()` for unit testing. Given the fix is 
a one-line typo correction and the controller already catches 
the invalid parameters, I believe the added complexity is not
justified. Happy to explore that path if reviewers feel otherwise.

title: Add support for generating linker section item count at build time
body:
Make it possible to calculate the number of items in the linker section at compile time instead of linking time.
This allows user to optimize the amount of space allocated when tracking the items stored in the linker section.

What this means in practice in the case of network interface count:

* Network interfaces are created using a macro by network device driver.
  The network interface structs are placed in the linker section where
  they are able to be traversed and read. There are no issues with this
  operation and network interfaces can be found at runtime correctly.
* If user wants to allocate enough space for tracking these network
  interface, currently user needs to either use malloc or guessing how
  many network interfaces there will be in the build and allocate
  enough space for network interface information (pointers for example)

With this change to `subsys/net/ip/CMakeLists.txt`
```
    include(gen_count)

    gen_section_count(
      TARGET          net_if
      SECTION         net_if_area
      ITEM_TYPE       "struct net_if"
      PRODUCER_TARGET ${ZEPHYR_CURRENT_LIBRARY}
      CONSUMERS       ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/net_if.c
    )
```
we are able to say in the application .c file
```
    /* Generated network interface count header */
    #include "net_if_count.h"

    static const struct net_if *ifaces[NET_IF_COUNT];
```
In this example, the value of `NET_IF_COUNT` is 4 and its information is found in the generated file
`build/zephyr/include/generated/zephyr/net_if_count.h` which looks like this
```
   /* AUTO-GENERATED by gen_section_count.py — do not edit */
   #ifndef NET_IF_COUNT_H
   #define NET_IF_COUNT_H

   /** Number of items in the 'net_if_area' linker section. */
   #define NET_IF_COUNT  (272U / sizeof(struct net_if))

   #endif /* NET_IF_COUNT_H */
```
This allows us to avoid using dynamic memory and always allocate enough space statically. We also do not need to overestimate the allocated section count either.

In application `CMakeLists.txt` file we just need to say so that if the network interface count changes, the system will re-compile the .c file automatically.
```
   include(gen_count)

   gen_section_count_add_consumer(
     TARGET  app
     HEADER  net_if
     FILES   ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/main.c
   )
```
During the linking of the application, this is seen
```
[141/144] Linking C executable zephyr/zephyr.elf
Generating files from build/zephyr/zephyr.elf for board: native_sim/native
  zephyr.elf: 'net_if_area' = 272 B  (merged section)
[gen_section_count] 'net_if_area': 272 B ->
                             build/zephyr/subsys/net/ip/net_if_count.h.tmp
-- gen_section_count [net_if]: count changed, updating header and
re-invoking build
[1/5] Building C object zephyr/subsys/net/ip/CMakeFiles/
                                         net_if_consumers.dir/net_if.c.obj
[2/5] Linking C static library zephyr/libzephyr.a
[3/5] Linking C executable zephyr/zephyr.elf
Generating files from build/zephyr/zephyr.elf for board: native_sim/native
  zephyr.elf: 'net_if_area' = 272 B  (merged section)
[gen_section_count] header unchanged — skipping write
[gen_section_count] 'net_if_area': 272 B ->
                             build/zephyr/subsys/net/ip/net_if_count.h.tmp
-- gen_section_count [net_if]: count unchanged
[4/5] Building native simulator runner, and linking final executable
[5/5] Running utility command for native_runner_executable
[143/144] cd build && build/zephyr/zephyr.exe
```

body: **Summary** This PR adds EFI GOP framebuffer display support for x86 EFI boot and enables running LVGL on top of the firmware-provided framebuffer without requiring external display hardware. The EFI stub now saves GOP framebuffer metadata for the kernel, and a new display driver exposes the framebuffer through Zephyr's display API. The driver validates GOP mode information, preserves the native framebuffer pixel order, and keeps a Zephyr-facing ARGB_8888 interface for LVGL integration. This change fills that gap and makes it possible to: - use the EFI-provided framebuffer directly - run LVGL on qemu_x86_64 with UEFI/OVMF - validate the full path with a dedicated sample **Testing** Tested with: - qemu_x86_64 - UEFI boot with OVMF - EFI GOP display enabled - sample: samples/drivers/efi_gop Verified: - system boots through UEFI - GOP framebuffer is detected - LVGL UI renders successfully - colors display correctly - QEMU UEFI graphical run path works as expected **How to run** Install the uefi-run fork with pflash support: ```sh cargo install --git https://github.com/rede97/uefi-run uefi-run ``` Then build and run: ```sh export OVMF_CODE_FD_PATH=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE_4M.fd export OVMF_VAR_FD_PATH=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS_4M.fd west build -b qemu_x86_64 samples/drivers/efi_gop/ -p always west build -t run ``` Screenshots

body:
Fixes #106450

### Problem
`CENTRAL_TRX_BUSY_ITERATION_MAX` and `PERIPHERAL_TRX_BUSY_ITERATION_MAX` are defined as `MIN(4U, EVENT_DEFER_MAX)`. When `EVENT_DEFER_MAX = 1`, this evaluates to `1`, causing debug asserts during normal operation.

### Root Cause
The TRX busy iteration limit is independent of `EVENT_DEFER_MAX`. Coupling them leads to unintended assert failures.

### Fix
Set both macros to the constant `4U`.

### Testing
Verified on nRF52840 central-peripheral connection; no assert triggered.

title: HX711 SPI Driver Bug?
body:
### Describe the bug

As weight is slowly applied to the load cell, readings ramp up normally, then
suddenly jump to zero or near-zero while weight is still being applied. Values
jump around erratically for a bit, then stabilize and return to normal
readings at higher weights. This behavior reproduces across multiple cells
(5 kg and 1 kg) and with a clamped test setup, ruling out hardware and
mechanical causes.  This is being built for a Raspberry Pi Pico and does not
appear to be a regression.

## Root Cause

The HX711 SPI driver (`zephyr/drivers/sensor/hx711_spi/hx711_spi.c`) has a
one-bit error in its sample extraction logic.

### How the driver works

The driver clocks the HX711 over SPI by sending `0xAA` (10101010) on MOSI,
which is wired to the HX711's PD_SCK pin. Each byte produces four PD_SCK
rising edges at MOSI bit positions 7, 5, 3, and 1. The HX711's DOUT (wired to
MISO) is valid at those same positions. Six bytes are sent, yielding
6 x 4 = 24 data bits.

### The bug

In `hx711_spi_read_sample()`, the bit extraction loop is:

```c
*sample <<= 4;
*sample |= (b & 0x1) | (((b >> 3) & 0x1) << 1) | (((b >> 5) & 0x1) << 2) |
           (((b >> 7) & 0x1) << 3);
```

This extracts MISO bits **7, 5, 3, 0**. Bit 0 is wrong -- it should be
bit 1.

MISO bit 0 is sampled when PD_SCK has just fallen (MOSI = 0). At that instant
the HX711 is transitioning DOUT to the *next* data bit. The captured value is
therefore either the old bit, the new bit, or metastable -- depending on
propagation timing. In practice, each nibble's LSB ends up being a copy of the
next nibble's MSB rather than the correct data bit.

### Impact

Every fourth bit in the 24-bit sample is corrupted (bit positions 0, 4, 8, 12,
16, 20). The maximum error from these six bits is:

    2^20 + 2^16 + 2^12 + 2^8 + 2^4 + 2^0 = 1,118,481 counts

out of a full-scale value of 8,388,607 (0x7FFFFF) -- roughly 13% of full
scale. Whether an error is visible depends on whether adjacent data bits
happen to match. At certain weight ranges the bits align and readings look
fine; at others they diverge, causing sudden jumps to zero or wild oscillation.

## Fix

Change `(b & 0x1)` to `((b >> 1) & 0x1)` so all four bits per byte are
extracted from the correct MISO positions (7, 5, 3, 1):

```c
*sample <<= 4;
*sample |= ((b >> 1) & 0x1) | (((b >> 3) & 0x1) << 1) |
           (((b >> 5) & 0x1) << 2) | (((b >> 7) & 0x1) << 3);
```



### Regression

- [ ] This is a regression.

### Steps to reproduce

Add the HX711 driver with an appropriate HX711 board and load cell, preferably with a proper test stand for the load cell.  As pressure is slowly added to the load cell values will begin to climb, then suddenly jump back to zero briefly, then appear to jump around at random.  As pressure slowly increases the numbers will suddenly stabilize for a while, then start jumping around again.  This is very consistent across multiple load cells of differing ranges. 

### Relevant log output

```shell
Difficult to provide log output for a physical device.
```

### Impact

Major – Severely degrades functionality; workaround is difficult or unavailable.

### Environment

Mac OS using the Zephyr SDK, version info below:

 git log --abbrev-commit --pretty=oneline -2
56f8a30c7fd (HEAD -> main, origin/main, origin/HEAD) Revert "tests: zbus: add multidomain proxy agent test suite"
82f9db67076 tests: zbus: ipc_backend: Fix string literal comparison warning

### Additional Context

Full disclosure, I used Claude Code to track down the apparent bug.  I'm using Zephyr to start brushing up on my very rusty C skills.  I have looked over the output of it's bug report and, to the best of my abilities, verified that it is correct in it's analysis.  Applying the fix that Claude supplied immediately fixed my issues with reading data from the load cell.

title: xtensa: fix memory domain lock inversion
body:
Fixes #106925.

## What changed

- stop taking `z_mem_domain_lock` inside `__arch_mem_map()`
- stop taking `z_mem_domain_lock` inside `__arch_mem_unmap()`
- document that `xtensa_mmu_lock` already serializes Xtensa domain-list walks and page-table updates in those helpers

## Why

`k_mem_domain_deinit()` takes `z_mem_domain_lock` and then reaches Xtensa code that takes `xtensa_mmu_lock` through `arch_mem_domain_deinit()`.

`arch_mem_map()` / `arch_mem_unmap()` already take `xtensa_mmu_lock` before calling into `__arch_mem_map()` / `__arch_mem_unmap()`, and those helpers were re-taking `z_mem_domain_lock` while walking `xtensa_domain_list`.

That creates an AB/BA lock-order inversion:

- `z_mem_domain_lock -> xtensa_mmu_lock`
- `xtensa_mmu_lock -> z_mem_domain_lock`

This change keeps `xtensa_mmu_lock` as the sole lock for the Xtensa domain-list walk and associated page-table updates in these helpers, avoiding the deadlock path.

## Validation

- inspected the current Xtensa memory-domain call paths around `arch_mem_map()`, `arch_mem_unmap()`, and `arch_mem_domain_deinit()`
- `git diff --check`

I could not run the Xtensa test matrix in this environment.

title: zephyr: drivers: wifi: infineon: wpa_supplicant support integration
body:
In this PR, added support for the wpa_supplicant interfacing to the infineon's wifi driver.

Here the major changes include adding capability, send_mlme, send_external_auth_status ops to the wifi driver. With this patch, the supplicant support for infineon driver is enabled.

Testing done : Verified Open, WPA2 and WPA3 connection using wpa_supplicant(through wifi-shell application).

Related supplicant zephyr PR - https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hostap/pull/132 

PR #107029 (Zephyr driver) implements the send_external_auth_status and send_mlme driver ops that PR #132 (hostap shim) calls — and PR #132 adds the ext_auth_req callback that PR #107029 invokes. Neither works without the other: the Zephyr driver alone has no SAE state machine, and the hostap shim alone has no driver ops to call into.

When the whd-expansion receives an SAE authentication frame, the driver receives it as a WHD event (WLC_E_EXT_AUTH_FRAME_RX). For WPA3, the driver cannot handle authentication itself; it must hand it off upward to wpa_supplicant. It does this by calling send_external_auth_status to report auth results back after supplicant completes the exchange, and by exposing send_mlme so supplicant can transmit SAE commit/confirm frames.

Signed-off-by: Ramprasad Kannappan [Ramprasad.Kannappan@infineon.com](mailto:Ramprasad.Kannappan@infineon.com)

title: drivers: flash: add single bank flash support for stm32g4x
body:
Currently the stm32g4x flash driver only works in dual bank for devices that support it. This is inconvenient when using mcuboot on a device with less than the maximum 512k of flash, as it creates an unaddressable "hole" between the two banks, artificially constraining the partition layout for the bootloader, primary, and upgrade slots. This PR updates the STM32G4 flash driver to add a runtime check to see if the device is configured in single bank or dual bank mode and adjust the page size accordingly. Devices in the STM32G4 family with Category 3 flash supporting dual-bank mode have a page size of 2kiB when configured in dual bank mode, or a page size of 4kiB when configured in single bank mode. When in single bank mode, the flash memory is contiguous regardless of the flash size. Note that the driver must do both a compile time and runtime check for dual bank configuration as dual bank mode is only supported on some devices in the family, and for those that do support dual bank mode, they may or may not be configured as such.

This change was tested on a custom board with an STM32G474RC MCU with 256kiB flash memory in both single and dual bank configurations, as well as on a Nucleo G431RB where the MCU uses category 2 flash memory only supporting single bank operation. title: usb: device_next: cdc: fix state cleanup in disable and update callbacks
body:
On self-powered USB devices, disconnecting and reconnecting the cable
triggers a disable/enable cycle. Several class drivers did not fully
reset their internal state during disable or alternate setting changes,
leading to failures on reconnection:

- **CDC-ECM/NCM**: `OUT_ENGAGED` not cleared in disable or update(alt=0).
  If `update(alt=1)` calls `out_start()` before the async `-ECONNABORTED`
  completion clears the flag, it returns `-EBUSY` silently and no OUT
  transfer is ever started -- the interface is permanently dead.

- **CDC-ECM/NCM**: `sync_sem` not signaled in disable. If a TX thread is
  blocked in `send()` waiting on `sync_sem`, the `-ECONNABORTED`
  completion for the IN endpoint normally signals it. An explicit
  `k_sem_give()` in disable provides a safety net. To prevent the give
  (or a later deferred completion) from leaving a stale semaphore token,
  `k_sem_reset()` is added in `update(alt=1)` before starting the next
  transfer cycle.

- **CDC-NCM**: `if_state` not reset in disable. The notification state
  machine could retain stale state across a disable/enable cycle.

- **CDC-ACM**: `CDC_ACM_RX_FIFO_BUSY` not cleared and `notif_sem` not
  signaled in disable, same pattern as ECM/NCM. `k_sem_reset()` in
  `enable()` drains any stale token.

## Background

Discovered while debugging permanent USB failure on a self-powered
nRF5340 device after VBUS disconnect/reconnect cycles. The primary
failure mode (buffer pool exhaustion from dropped transfer completions)
was already fixed in Zephyr 4.4 by commit 5137439a476 ("usb: device_next:
use slist to store completed transfer requests"). These class-level
fixes are defense-in-depth -- the disable callback should clean up all
class state regardless of whether the completion mechanism works
correctly.

## Test plan
- [x] Before/after fix verified on Zephyr 4.3: VBUS stress test on
  nRF5340 reproduced permanent OUT_ENGAGED failure without fix, passed
  with fix applied
- [x] On Zephyr 4.4.0-rc3 (which has the slist fix), the root cause no
  longer reproduces, but these fixes ensure correct state cleanup as
  defense-in-depth
- [x] CDC-ECM: 100/100 VBUS power cycles pass on nRF5340 DK (zperf
  sample, v4.4.0-rc3 + fixes, CoolGear managed USB hub)
- [x] CDC-NCM: 100/100 VBUS power cycles pass on nRF5340 DK (zperf
  sample, v4.4.0-rc3 + fixes, CoolGear managed USB hub)
- [x] Confirmed on ADT-25 custom board (nRF5340, CDC-ECM + CDC-NCM +
  CDC-ACM composite) with Zephyr 4.3 + backported fixes
- [x] CI build validation

title: scripts: build: fix ULEB128 decoding in gen_kobject_list.py
body:
The DW_OP_plus_uconst offset in DWARF location expressions is ULEB128-encoded, but the script reads only a single byte. This silently truncates offsets >= 128, registering kernel objects at wrong addresses in the kobject hash table.

Clang triggers this because it emits DW_OP_addr + DW_OP_plus_uconst for variables within structs, while GCC emits a direct DW_OP_addr.

title: usb: cdc_ecm/cdc_ncm: make remote MAC address descriptor mutable
body:
## Summary

Fixes #107130.

The USB CDC-ECM and CDC-NCM drivers currently bake the remote (host-side) MAC address into a `static const` string descriptor at build time via `USBD_DESC_STRING_DEFINE`, making it immutable at runtime. The local MAC can be changed via `ETHERNET_CONFIG_TYPE_MAC_ADDRESS`, but the remote MAC cannot — so production devices sharing one firmware image end up with identical host-side MACs, causing ARP confusion on shared hosts/networks.

This series:

- Replaces the static const descriptor buffer with a `static uint8_t[13]` mutable buffer + a hand-rolled `struct usbd_desc_node` pointing at it (no changes to `struct usbd_desc_node` or any USB stack APIs).
- Adds a small helper that derives the remote MAC from the local MAC by flipping the U/L bit (byte 0 XOR 0x02) and formats it as uppercase hex.
- Calls the helper from `preinit()` and from `set_config(ETHERNET_CONFIG_TYPE_MAC_ADDRESS)` so runtime MAC changes propagate automatically to the host-visible `iMACAddress` string.

No new public API, no DTS binding changes, and backward compatible — devices that don't change the MAC at runtime behave identically to before.

Split into two commits (one per driver) for reviewability; the change is symmetric.

## Test plan

- [ ] Boot with `remote-mac-address` from DTS — host sees the DTS-derived remote MAC (U/L bit flipped from local).
- [ ] Change local MAC at runtime via `NET_REQUEST_ETHERNET_SET_MAC_ADDRESS`, re-enumerate, confirm host sees updated remote MAC string.
- [ ] Two devices with same image but unique hardware-derived MACs enumerate with distinct remote MACs on the same host.
- [ ] Repeat for both CDC-ECM and CDC-NCM.

title: usb: device_next: cdc_ecm/cdc_ncm: make iMACAddress descriptor dynamic
body:
## Summary

Fixes #107130.

USB CDC-ECM and CDC-NCM advertise a remote (host-side) MAC address via the `iMACAddress` string descriptor, which today is baked into flash at build time from the `remote-mac-address` DT property. Devices sharing one firmware image therefore end up with identical host-side MACs on shared hosts and networks, even when they carry unique local MACs derived from hardware identifiers at runtime.

### Design

Introduce a `USBD_DUT_STRING_MAC_ADDRESS` string descriptor usage type and a `USBD_DESC_MAC_ADDRESS_DEFINE()` helper that binds a descriptor node to a *live 6-byte MAC buffer*. At `GET_DESCRIPTOR` time the device stack reads the current local MAC from the buffer, flips the U/L bit to obtain the host-side MAC, and renders a 12-character uppercase-hex ASCII string.

This mirrors the existing pull-model renderer used for HWINFO-derived serial numbers (`USBD_DUT_STRING_SERIAL_NUMBER` + `use_hwinfo`): `dn->ptr` stays `const void *const` and the class driver does not need to track or re-render the descriptor when the local MAC changes. Single source of truth (`data->mac_addr[6]`), no push-model bookkeeping, no drift risk. The byte-to-hex loop shared by both renderers is factored into a `bytes_to_ascii_hex_upper()` helper.

### Backward compatibility

The `remote-mac-address` DT property is **deprecated, not removed**:

- If set → legacy build-time static string is preserved (unchanged behaviour).
- If omitted → new dynamic derivation is used.

In-tree samples and tests drop the property so they exercise the new default path. Downstream overlays that set it continue to work and see a DT deprecation warning.

### Why this shape

Considered three approaches:

1. **Push-model mutable buffer in the class driver** — class pre-renders the string on every MAC mutation. Requires a writable alias that cheats around `const void *const ptr`, and every code path that touches `mac_addr` must remember to re-render → drift risk.
2. **HWINFO-style pull renderer** (this PR) — stack-side dispatch per utype; class driver owns only the canonical MAC; renderer reads it on demand. Additive, preserves `const`, mirrors existing precedent.
3. **Generic descriptor-provider callback** — right long-term shape once ≥3 dynamic-string consumers exist, but premature for N=2.

(2) is strictly better than (1) on drift-safety, const-correctness, and bookkeeping; and strictly cheaper than (3) on time-to-merge for the same correctness properties. A follow-up RFC for (3) can be filed once a third consumer appears.

## Test plan

- [ ] Boot with no `remote-mac-address` overlay — host sees iMACAddress = local MAC with U/L bit flipped, uppercase hex.
- [ ] Boot with `remote-mac-address` still set in overlay — host sees the legacy static string; DT deprecation warning appears at build.
- [ ] Change local MAC at runtime via `NET_REQUEST_ETHERNET_SET_MAC_ADDRESS`, re-enumerate, confirm host sees updated remote MAC string (dynamic path only).
- [ ] Two devices with the same image but unique hardware-derived MACs enumerate with distinct remote MACs on the same host.
- [ ] Regression: HWINFO serial number descriptor still renders correctly (shared `bytes_to_ascii_hex_upper` path).
- [ ] Repeat for both CDC-ECM and CDC-NCM.

title: arm: cortex_m: call arch_data_copy before fault handlers in TF-M NS builds
body:
## Summary

On TF-M Non-Secure builds, if a fault fires inside `__start` before `z_prep_c()` has run, the `.data` section in SRAM contains uninitialized values. The fault handler's logging path (`log_panic()` → `mpsc_pbuf_alloc()` → `get_skip()`) dereferences `.data` variables containing garbage, causing a secondary fault that masks the original fault's PC and CFSR.

This was discovered during STM32H563 bring-up — every NS boot fault appeared as an SAU attribution violation at a random address in Secure flash, with no useful diagnostic information.

## Changes

- Call `arch_data_copy()` immediately after MSP setup in `reset.S`, guarded by `CONFIG_BUILD_WITH_TFM`
- `z_prep_c` calls `arch_data_copy` again later; repeating is idempotent
- `arch_bss_zero` is deliberately not called here because `z_main_stack` (which MSP points into) lives in BSS

## Test plan

- [ ] Boot a TF-M NS image on STM32H563 with an intentional fault in `__start`
- [ ] Verify fault handler prints the actual fault PC and CFSR instead of a secondary SAU violation

title: drivers: i3c: i3c_dw: implement recover_bus callback and fix stale state after re-DAA
body:
Implement .recover_bus for both the i3c and i2c_api entries in the DesignWare I3C driver so that i3c_recover_bus() and the i3c shell can actually recover a stuck bus. Previously, the callback was not wired up, and calls returned -ENOSYS.

The implementation deliberately avoids RESET_CTRL_SOFT and the RESET_CTRL_ALL superset because they clear the Device Address Table (DAT) and Device Characteristic Table (DCT), destroying the driver-to-hardware mapping for attached targets. Instead, the recovery path:

  - drains any pending IBIs that could block a resume,
  - flushes the command, response, RX, TX, and IBI queues,
  - asserts DEV_CTRL_RESUME to clear a halt caused by a prior transfer error.

This is the same FIFO flush + RESUME sequence already used by the driver's per-transfer error path, so the safety properties are well understood. The operation is mutex-protected to avoid race conditions with in-flight transfers.

The DesignWare I3C controller driver maintained several pieces of
per-target state that went out of sync with hardware whenever DAA ran
more than once on the same bus (e.g., boot DAA, RSTDAA + DAA, or a
second explicit i3c_do_daa() call).This desynchronization between
software state and hardware resulted in persistent -ENXIO errors
on all transfers after bus re-enumeration.

Root cause (shared by all three fixes below):

The DW controller's ENTDAA implementation treats DAT slots as a free
pool. It fills empty slots starting at COMMAND_PORT_DEV_INDEX in
arbitration order (lowest PID wins first). This order is unrelated to
the slot chosen by dw_i3c_attach_device() at subsystem init. The driver
previously assumed the attach-time binding was stable across DAA
cycles and never re-read hardware state; any target that participated
in ENTDAA (i.e., had no "assigned-address" in DT, or lost its DA via
RSTDAA) ended up with desc->controller_priv pointing to one DAT slot
while hardware had placed the target in another.

Three related issues are fixed together:

1. add_slave_from_daa() did not refresh BCR/DCR on re-DAA. The I3C
   spec allows a target to publish different BCR/DCR after a reset,
   and after RSTDAA the cached values may no longer reflect the
   target's current capabilities. Always re-read from the Device
   Characteristic Table when a new DA is assigned.

2. add_slave_from_daa() did not detect the priv->id != pos case
   described above. When it occurs (the common case for any DT
   target without "assigned-address"), rebind controller_priv to
   the DAT slot hardware chose and return the old slot to the free
   pool. Without this, subsequent transfers write the command DAT
   index of an empty slot and NACK with -ENXIO.

3. dw_i3c_device_find() only searched the static dev_list built
   from DT. Targets allocated dynamically for non-DT devices on the
   bus were invisible to PID lookups, so add_slave_from_daa() kept
   allocating fresh descriptors on every DAA cycle and eventually
   exhausted the descriptor pool. Fall back to scanning the
   attached-device runtime list by PID when the static lookup
   misses.

i3c_bus_rstdaa_all() sends the RSTDAA broadcast and clears every
attached descriptor's dynamic_addr, but does not return those
addresses to the address-slot pool. Subsequent calls to
i3c_addr_slots_next_free_find() therefore skip the freed DAs and
the bus monotonically exhausts the valid dynamic-address range
across successive RSTDAA + DAA cycles.

Free each target's DA in the address-slot bookkeeping in the same
loop that clears dynamic_addr, so RSTDAA is fully reversible at
the software level.

This fixes sustained RSTDAA+DAA test cycles across all I3C
controller drivers (cadence, dw, mcux, max32, stm32, npcx,
renesas, it51xxx). Previously, after ~10-20 RSTDAA cycles the
bus would run out of assignable dynamic addresses.

title: drivers: Add pse84 autanalog PRB reference
labels: area: Devicetree Binding;area: Regulators;platform: Infineon;area: MFD;area: Boards/SoCs;AI-assisted
body:
Added support for autanalog PRB for PSE84.

This uses the autonomous controller implemented in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/106227 .

The PRB is a programmable reference block inside the autonomous (aut) analog subsystem. It is controlled using the autonomous controller (AC), which is a programmable state machine. The AC is shared across all autonomous analog peripherals including the SAR, PRB, PTComp, CTB, and CTDAC.

The PRB contains two variable voltage references derived from either VDDA(1.8V) or VGBR(0.9V). These need to be configured together and accessed using the AC. title: ADC Channel Address Mismatch
labels: priority: low;area: ADC;platform: STM32;platform: NXP;platform: Microchip SAM;Stale;platform: Nuvoton;platform: Infineon;area: Board/SoC configuration;platforms: Renesas RZ;platform: Arduino
body:
### Describe the bug

A change was made in in the ADC API in PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/99120 that changed the `ADC_CHANNEL_DT_NODE` behavior.  

Old macro implementation: 
```
 #define ADC_CHANNEL_DT_NODE(ctlr, input) \
     DT_FOREACH_CHILD_VARGS(ctlr, ADC_FOREACH_INPUT, input)
 
 #define ADC_FOREACH_INPUT(node, input) \
     IF_ENABLED(IS_EQ(DT_REG_ADDR_RAW(node), input), (node))
```
In this implementation, the child node's reg property was used in the comparison with input in the macro.  

New macro implementation: 
```
 #define ADC_CHANNEL_DT_NODE(ctlr, input) \
     DT_CHILD_BY_UNIT_ADDR_INT(ctlr, input)
```
In the new implementation, the child node is looked up using the unit address.  

Now for the problem:
In a number of devices, this address is defined as a decimal value when it should be defined as a hex value.  Example from the kit_psc3m5_evk overlay from the adc_dt sample, which results in a reg value of 12, but an address of 18:
```
	channel@12 {
		reg = <12>;
		zephyr,acquisition-time = <ADC_ACQ_TIME_DEFAULT>;
		zephyr,gain = "ADC_GAIN_1";
		zephyr,reference = "ADC_REF_INTERNAL";
		zephyr,resolution = <12>;
	};
```

I can only verify the problem on the Infineon kit_psc3m5_evk board, but I believe the following overlays suffer from the same bug:  
 - `samples/drivers/adc/adc_dt/boards/kit_psc3m5_evk.overlay`
 - `samples/drivers/adc/adc_dt/boards/saml21_xpro.overlay`
 - `samples/drivers/adc/adc_dt/boards/rzt2m_rsk_r9a07g075m24gbg_cr520.overlay`
 - `samples/drivers/adc/adc_dt/boards/arduino_uno_r4.overlay`
 - `samples/drivers/adc/adc_sequence/boards/kit_psc3m5_evk.overlay`
 - `samples/subsys/usb_c/sink/boards/numaker_m2l31ki.overlay`
 - `tests/drivers/adc/adc_accuracy_test/boards/frdm_kl25z.overlay`
 - `tests/drivers/adc/adc_api/boards/kit_psc3m5_evk.overlay`
 - `tests/drivers/adc/adc_error_cases/boards/kit_psc3m5_evk.overlay`
 - `tests/drivers/dac/dac_loopback/nxp-dac0-adc23-internal.overlay`
 - `tests/drivers/dac/dac_loopback/boards/stm32l562e_dk.overlay`

### Regression

Could not setup channel #2 (-134)
```

title: build: Consolidate EDT-Derived Build Outputs in `gen_edt.py`
body:
Closes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/107494

### Problem Description

Every Zephyr build runs the devicetree configuration pipeline, and that pipeline currently launches multiple Python processes to produce artifacts derived from the same devicetree data.

Today, the build constructs an EDT object, serializes it to `edt.pickle`, and then runs follow-up Python scripts to generate artifacts such as `Kconfig.dts`, `devicetree_generated.h`, and `edt.pickle.cmake`. These later steps either reload the pickled EDT or independently inspect devicetree bindings. That means the build repeatedly pays Python startup, import, and data reconstruction costs during CMake configure.

This RFC proposes consolidating those outputs into the existing `gen_edt.py` step, so the artifacts can be emitted from the EDT object while it is already available in memory.

The goal is to reduce the amount of Python work performed during CMake configuration, a path executed by every Zephyr build.

### Proposed Change (Summary)

I propose we consolidate Python processes such that `gen_edt.py` generates:
-  `devicetree_generated.h`
- `edt.pickle`
- `edt.pickle.cmake`
- `Kconfig.dts`
- `zephyr.dts`

Today, `gen_edt.py` generates `edt.pickle` and `zephyr.dts`.

The work done by `gen_edt.py` today already contains all the needed information to generate `Kconfig.dts` required to finish the build. The only difference is `gen_edt.py` does not parse **all** the binding files in the tree, instead it only looks up compatibles which are required by the device tree for the respective image being built.

Benefits:
* Faster builds ~600ms on my end (depends on the machine)

#### Benchmarks

I used the following command on Ubuntu 26.04

```
hyperfine --shell=none --warmup 2 --runs 10 "west build --pristine always --board nrf52dk/nrf52832 samples/basic/blinky --cmake-only"
```

main (32e0ab566c6ce6e9fe28e5eed901ce19c21f92b5):
```
Benchmark 1: west build --pristine always --board nrf52dk/nrf52832 samples/basic/blinky --cmake-only
  Time (mean ± σ):      6.452 s ±  0.064 s    [User: 5.211 s, System: 1.246 s]
  Range (min … max):    6.350 s …  6.555 s    10 runs
```

PR branch:
```
Benchmark 1: west build --pristine always --board nrf52dk/nrf52832 samples/basic/blinky --cmake-only
  Time (mean ± σ):      5.845 s ±  0.058 s    [User: 4.685 s, System: 1.167 s]
  Range (min … max):    5.779 s …  5.955 s    10 runs
```

This reduces the measured configure-only pristine build time from 6.452s to 5.845s on my machine.

### Proposed Change (Detailed)

The existing output formatting logic in `gen_driver_kconfig_dts.py`, `gen_defines.py`, and `gen_dts_cmake.py` is refactored into reusable writer helpers. The standalone scripts remain available where needed, but the normal build path can call those helpers from `gen_edt.py` using the already-constructed EDT object.

The CMake integration is updated accordingly. `dts_edt_pickle()` in `dts.cmake` invokes `gen_edt.py` with output paths for the additional generated files listed above, and the separate `dts_gen_driver_kconfig()` and `dts_gen_defines()` steps are removed. 

`zephyr_dt_import()` in `extensions.cmake` accepts a new optional pre-generated `edt.pickle.cmake` file and includes it directly. If the optional argument is not used, then the previous behavior is used where `edt.pickle.cmake` is generated using `edt.pickle`.

* Add the following new arguments to `gen_edt.py` script:
  * `--edt-pickle`: Path to an already available `edt.pickle` file. This is useful for example when we only need to generate `edt.pickle.cmake`.
  * `--kconfig-out`: Path to write `Kconfig.dts` file. Unlike the standalone compliance use case, the normal build path would generate this from the current EDT, so it only contains compatibles present in the devicetree being built.
  * `--cmake-out`: Path to write `edt.pickle.cmake` file
  * `--header-out`: Path to write `devicetree_generated.h`

### Dependencies

* Compliance Test in CI Github Actions should still continue to parse all binding files, so we cannot remove `gen_driver_kconfig_dts.py`.
* Some documentation will need to be updated. Like: https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/build/dts/dt-vs-kconfig.html#automatic-kconfig-symbols-from-devicetree
* There are some documentation pages related to `gen_defines.py` which may need to be updated.

### Concerns and Unresolved Questions

* Rename `gen_edt.py` to something else?

### Alternatives Considered

A few attempts have been made to optimize  `gen_driver_kconfig_dts.py`.

* https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/103660
* https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/101383

title: drivers: i2c: i2c_dw: fix slave-mode ISR state races and missing START_DET unmask
body:
Fixes three in DesignWare I2C slave mode that broke the Zephyr
I2C target API contract.
 
1. Unmask START_DET for the slave so fresh START conditions reset slave
    state correctly. RESTART detection for same-address repeated starts
    is not supported by the IP (RESTART_DET is not synthesized and
    START_DET does not fire while the slave remains continuously
    addressed); applications must rely on STOP_DET for transaction 
    boundaries in that case.
 
2. Use cached intr_stat in i2c_dw_slave_read_clear_intr_bits()
   The helper re-read IC_INTR_STAT while the ISR had already cached
   it. Bits asserted between the two reads caused the helper and the ISR
   to see different states, producing spurious write_requested()
   calls on aborted transactions.
 
3. Clear read_in_progress on all transaction boundaries
   Previously, only cleared on stop_det. On error paths (tx_abrt,
   rx_under/over, tx_over, rx_done) and new-transaction paths
   (start_det, gen_call) the flag stayed true, so the next read
   skipped read_requested() and delivered the first byte via
   read_processed().

Fixes: #111412

title: drivers: uhc: max3421e: respect xfer->mps for short-packet detection
body:
The MAX3421E driver hardcodes MAX3421E_MAX_EP_SIZE (64) as the short-packet threshold for IN transfers and as the chunk size for OUT transfers, ignoring the endpoint's actual max packet size already provided in xfer->mps.

For Full-Speed devices reporting bMaxPacketSize0 != 64 on EP0 (8, 16 or 32 are all permitted by USB 2.0), every full-MPS packet is wrongly treated as a short packet and the IN transfer ends after the first packet. The remaining bytes of the device descriptor are never read, so the upper layer sees bNumConfigurations == 0 and enumeration fails.

Pass the full uhc_transfer to max3421e_xfer_data() so both the OUT chunk size and the BULKIN end-of-transfer condition honor xfer->mps. When xfer->mps is zero, fall back to
MAX3421E_MAX_EP_SIZE to keep existing behavior.

title: modbus: rtu: fix buffer overrun in cb_handler_rx
body:
## Summary

`cb_handler_rx()` in `subsys/modbus/modbus_serial.c` uses strict equality (`==`) to check whether `uart_buf[]` is full. If `uart_buf_ctr` ever advances past `CONFIG_MODBUS_BUFFER_SIZE` by even one byte — for any reason — the equality misses forever, `modbus_serial_rx_disable()` is never called again, and every subsequent received byte is written to `*uart_buf_ptr++` at an unbounded offset, silently corrupting adjacent static data.

This PR:

1. Changes the bounds check from `==` to `>=` so the disable still fires on any overshoot, regardless of how the counter got past the buffer size.
2. Loops `uart_fifo_read()` until it returns fewer bytes than requested, per the documented Zephyr UART API contract in `include/zephyr/drivers/uart.h`: *"once uart_irq_rx_ready() is detected, uart_fifo_read() must be called until it reads all available data in the FIFO."*
3. Bails on a negative return from `uart_fifo_read()` (the documented `-ENOSYS` / `-ENOTSUP` cases) without advancing buffer state.

## Field reproducer

Observed on an nRF9151 product reading Modbus RTU over RS485 with an auto-direction transceiver (no DE/RE# pin exposed) that echoes every transmitted byte back into RX. With back-to-back probes and short inter-frame gaps, the RX buffer overflowed before the RTU inter-frame timer fired, the bounds check was bypassed, and `uart_buf_ptr` walked past `uart_buf[]` into the adjacent `timestamp_func` symbol in the logging subsystem's `.data`. The next `LOG_*()` `BLX`'d a garbage address and faulted.

The exact mechanism by which `uart_buf_ctr` overshot 256 on this configuration (`CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN=y` with `uart_nrfx_uarte`) is not fully pinned down — `uarte_nrfx_fifo_read()` reads at most one byte per call, so a spec-compliant driver should not advance the counter by more than 1 per IRQ. The `>=` change catches the overshoot regardless of cause and was sufficient to eliminate the field crash; the drain loop separately makes the code conform to the documented API contract.

## Impact

Affects any Zephyr Modbus RTU user where `uart_buf_ctr` can ever cross `CONFIG_MODBUS_BUFFER_SIZE` — most plausibly on auto-direction RS485 transceivers where self-echo makes high-rate fill paths reachable on otherwise idle buses.

## Test plan

- [x] Built on nRF9151; the prior `SECURE_FAULT` is no longer reproducible on the same hardware and Modbus traffic pattern that previously triggered it reliably within minutes.
- [ ] No unit test added — the bug requires an early-missed overrun or a long-running burst that the current Modbus test fixtures do not produce. Open to suggestions on a mock UART driver setup.

Signed-off-by: Diego Solano <diegosolano@gmail.com>

title: cbprintf: guard append_string against NULL string pointers
body:
## Summary

Add a NULL guard at the top of `append_string()` in `lib/os/cbprintf_packaged.c` that substitutes the string \`\"(null)\"\` when a NULL pointer is passed. This matches the behavior of glibc's printf family and prevents a hard crash in the deferred-logging path.

## Background

Passing `NULL` to `%s` is a caller bug. But deferred/packaged logging (which is what `cbvprintf_package()` implements) captures the argument now and calls `strlen()` on it much later, during log processing. That splits the crash site from the buggy call, producing faults that appear to originate from the logging subsystem and making the bad caller very hard to identify.

On targets without memory protection this is undefined behavior (and usually a crash on the `strlen`). On Cortex-M33 targets using TF-M, the SPU catches the read at address 0 and raises `SECURE_FAULT`, which aborts the image.

## Why defensive, not strict

Two reasons to substitute rather than return an error:

1. glibc and musl both substitute \`\"(null)\"\` for NULL in `%s` — Zephyr diverging from that makes portable code harder to reason about.
2. The resulting log line includes the source filename/line (via the package metadata) and \`\"(null)\"\` makes the buggy caller trivially findable. Today the caller is invisible because the image dies mid-log.

I am not arguing that passing NULL to `%s` should be supported; I am arguing that the deferred logging infrastructure should fail gracefully when a caller does. If maintainers prefer to keep the strict UB behavior, I am happy to close this and instead hunt down and fix the NCS callers that passed NULL (one is in `nrf_modem_lib` around AT command log lines, based on my debugging).

## Reproducer

Observed on nRF9151 with TF-M and `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_DEFERRED=y`. An NCS module's log call passed a NULL `char *` to `%s`; the resulting `SECURE_FAULT` aborted the image. The crash traceback pointed at `cbprintf_package_convert()`, not at the caller.

## Test plan

- [x] Built with `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_DEFERRED=y` on nRF9151 + TF-M; log lines that previously crashed now print \`\"(null)\"\` and execution continues.
- [ ] No unit test added; happy to write one for `tests/unit/cbprintf/` exercising the NULL path if reviewers want.

Signed-off-by: Diego Solano <diegosolano@gmail.com>

title: Fix getaddrinfo() DNS retry handling
body:
**Summary**
Fix getaddrinfo() DNS retry handling to prevent crash on repeated DNS timeouts and to report temporary resolver exhaustion correctly.

**Root Cause**
When DNS was unavailable, getaddrinfo() retried after k_sem_take() timeout without always canceling the previous in-flight DNS query first.

getaddrinfo_state is stack-allocated and passed as DNS callback user_data. A delayed callback could execute after timeout/retry progression and touch stale state (k_sem_give(&state->sem)), which can corrupt kernel wait-list state and crash in scheduler/list code (sys_dlist_remove / k_sem_give path in sysworkq).

At the same time, unresolved pending queries could temporarily exhaust DNS query slots, returning -EAGAIN from resolver internals; this was previously mapped to DNS_EAI_SYSTEM (-11) instead of DNS_EAI_AGAIN (-3).

**Changes**
subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c
Cancel timed-out DNS query before retry.
Reset semaphore before retry.
Map resolver-side -EAGAIN to DNS_EAI_AGAIN (instead of generic DNS_EAI_SYSTEM).
User-visible Effect
No crash during prolonged DNS unavailability.
Temporary DNS pressure now reports DNS_EAI_AGAIN consistently.
Fewer misleading -11 (DNS_EAI_SYSTEM) results for retryable conditions.
**Validation**.
DNS-unavailable scenario now follows retry/error path without reproducing the previous crash pattern.

Fixes: #110771

labels: area: Timer;platform: NXP;area: Devicetree Binding;platform: NXP MCU;area: Boards/SoCs
body:
Add a system clock driver built on top of the NXP System Counter (SYS_CTR) block, which provides a 56-bit free-running counter and two compare frames capable of generating maskable interrupts.
 
System  counter is a free-running counter paired with an absolute compare register. Compare frame 0 is used for
the system timer, leaving frame 1 available for other consumers. The instance is selected via the zephyr,system-timer chosen property.

title: drivers: spi: spi_dw: add TI SSP frame format support
body:
The DesignWare SSI controller supports both Motorola SPI and TI SSP frame formats via the CTRLR0.FRF field, but the driver previously hard-coded Motorola and silently ignored the SPI_FRAME_FORMAT_TI flag.

Program CTRLR0.FRF based on config->operation. When TI SSP is selected, skip CPOL/CPHA programming since SCPH and SCPOL have no meaning in that format per the DW SSI databook.

Define FRF field positions for both the standard and HSSI variants of the IP, matching the existing +2 offset pattern used for SCPH, SCPOL, TMOD, SLV_OE and SRL.

title: net: dns: fix unpack of DNS record with multiple questions
body:
This pull request addresses issues with respect to handling of multi-question DNS queries. The issues were observed, when an external device performs a multi-question DNS query including name compressions. The individual questions are not properly parsed, typically only the first 2 were processed correctly.

The first issue is that the query offset was not properly updated.

The second issue relates to the use of message compression in domain names
(https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035#section-4.1.4). The pointers can be nested (i.e. a first pointer pointing to a label with another pointer)
For example: _http._tcp.local can be represented via: '_http' + (pointer to a '_tcp' label + (pointer to a 'local' label). This was not properly implemented, only single-pointers were properly supported.

title: CI: Overhaul testplan discovery on pull requests
labels: area: Kernel;area: Tests;area: Interrupt Controller;area: Continuous Integration;area: Testsuite;area: Linters
body:
Major overhaul of the test plan discovery and test selection logic in CI. The
new system is more modular and allows for more flexible test selection based on
various criteria.

Simple and trivial changes that would block ~10 runners are now handled by a
much more efficient test selection process, which should significantly reduce
the time it takes to run CI for small changes.


Try it out on commit ranges in your branch or main tree and examine test
selection, provide feedback here or in the PR.

```
./scripts/ci/test_plan_v2.py --help
./scripts/ci/test_plan_v2.py -c HEAD~10..HEAD
```


Add scripts/ci/test_plan_v2.py, a modular CI test-selection
tool that analyses the files changed in a Pull Request and emits a
targeted twister test plan, avoiding tests unrelated to the change
while maximising coverage of what was touched.

Architecture
============
A pipeline of independent strategies each receives the full (or
remaining) list of changed files and returns a list of TwisterCall
descriptors.  An Orchestrator executes the calls, merges results,
removes duplicates and writes testplan.json.  A shared PipelineContext
carries cross-strategy state (complexity score, per-file metrics).

Strategies (execution order)
=============================
0. ComplexityStrategy – analyses patchset complexity with pydriller
   (commit-level churn, changed-method CCN, DMM unit-complexity) and
   lizard (avg CCN delta between old and new file versions).  Emits a
   composite score into PipelineContext; no twister calls generated.

1. IgnoreStrategy – reads scripts/ci/twister_ignore.txt and silently
   consumes files matching any glob pattern (docs, tooling, workflows).

2. DirectTestStrategy – for files under tests/ or samples/, walks up
   to the nearest testcase.yaml/sample.yaml root and runs that exact
   suite with --integration.

3. SnippetStrategy – for files under snippets/, reads the snippet name
   from snippet.yml, finds tests that declare it as required_snippets
   and runs those test roots.

4. BoardStrategy – for files under boards/, enumerates all board
   variants via list_boards.py (including twister.yaml consolidated
   boards) and runs tests/integration/kernel on each variant.

5. SoCStrategy – for files under soc/, resolves SoC names from
   soc.yml, finds boards referencing those SoCs and runs
   tests/integration/kernel on them.

6. ManifestStrategy – for changed west.yml / submanifests files, diffs
   old vs new revision via git show, identifies added/removed/updated
   projects and runs --tag <module> --integration.

7. DriverCompatStrategy – for driver source files, extracts
   DT_DRV_COMPAT, finds test overlays that instantiate the compatible
   and adds those test directories as -T roots.

8. DtsBindingStrategy – for changed dts/bindings YAML files, reads the
   compatible: field and feeds it through the same compat-resolution
   chain as DriverCompatStrategy.

9. KconfigImpactStrategy – for changed Kconfig files and defconfigs,
   extracts symbol names and greps tests for .conf/.yaml files that
   enable those symbols.

10. HeaderImpactStrategy – for changed public headers, greps for
    #include users and maps them back to MAINTAINERS areas with tests.

11. MaintainerAreaStrategy – catch-all: matches remaining files against
    MAINTAINERS.yml areas and uses their tests: list.

RiskClassifierStrategy is implemented but disabled pending further
tuning of its classification rules.  When enabled it reads the
complexity score from PipelineContext to escalate NORMAL-risk files to
WIDE coverage when the score exceeds the threshold.

Output
======
* testplan.json – loaded by twister via --load-tests
* .testplan     – env-var file (TWISTER_TESTS, TWISTER_NODES,
                  TWISTER_FULL) consumed by CI orchestration


Fixes #8626
Resolves #100898

body:
Disable the second uart in the xterm-native-shell overlay (we do not need to UARTS, but having them both connected will confuse users)

Fix the run-bsim script. It had rotten and had quite many issues, let's fix them:

* Fix the build command example so it actually builds and is configured in a sensible way given how this script uses the executable (if we attach to the uart a terminal it should be in its own pty) (there is no global xterm-native-shell snippet)
* When stopping a possible previous bsim simulation, let's only stop the one we launch from this script, not any running in the computer
* Do not run the bsim handbrake from inside their artifacts folders, but from the installation folder (BSIM_OUT_PATH/bin)
* Add a timeout to stop the simulation after 1 hour so it does not linger forever
* Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH, as we are running the device .exe from an arbitrary folder
* Use the Execute bsim shell utility function, so we stop all programs in the background with Ctrl+C instead of letting them linger.
* Add explanation of the used command line parameters
* In the parameters to zephyr.exe:
  * Do not set the random seed unnecessarily (it is already a valid value)
  * Do not ask to wait for something to attach to the uart (we are telling the executable to automatically do it)
  * Set a small maxium synchronization delay with the phy (10ms) so the simulation appears fluid for interactive use
* Don't pushd when changing directory, we are in a subshell and will not popd
* Set the handbrake in actual real time instead of 10x. Set a small period for the handbrake, so the simulation feels fluid.
* Add a call wait_for_background_jobs so we wait for all programs in the background.

body:
Introduce mandatory fields that drivers need to include in their common data & config structs. These enable having a larger common functional layer between HCI drivers and their users, which in turn helps simplify drivers but also give the flexibility of introducing new functionality without breaking drivers or their users.

One first feature that gets moved into the common structs is the `recv` callback, along with a new `bt_hci_recv()` API that drivers use instead of directly having access to the callback.

The config common struct gets a `quirks` member, which isn't of much value now, but it's there to satisfy the C standard's requirement of non-empty structs, and also facilitate an easier transition to multi-controller support in the host (worked on in a separate PR)

title: Introduce clock monitor device driver api
labels: area: Samples;RFC;platform: NXP;area: Tests;area: Clock Control;area: Devicetree Binding;platform: NXP MCU;Release
body:
### What is Clock Monitor
A clock monitor is a small hardware block that watches one clock against another - either continuously checking that the monitored clock stays inside a programmable upper/lower frequency window, or counting it for a fixed number of reference cycles to report the measured frequency in Hz, or simply detecting that it has stopped. Most automotive and safety-grade MCUs ship one or more of these monitors so that a runaway, drifted, or stuck clock can be caught before it corrupts a peripheral or a control loop.

The core of the `clock_monitor` subsystem includes:
1. Two operating modes - WINDOW (threshold check) and MEASURE (frequency measurement
2. An event bitmap (FREQ_HIGH, FREQ_LOW, CLOCK_LOST, MEASURE_DONE) delivered through the configure-time callback; the most recent measurement result additionally remains retrievable by polling clock_monitor_get_rate().

### Practical Uses of Clock Monitor
In safety-critical applications (motor control, BMS, ADAS sensor fusion, etc.), the system clock and key peripheral clocks must stay within a known window for the control loop to behave correctly. A drifted or stuck clock can manifest as a wrong PWM duty cycle, a CAN bit-time error, or a missed control deadline - failures that are catastrophic for the system and very hard to diagnose after the fact. By configuring a clock monitor with the nominal frequency and a tolerance, the MCU can either raise an early-warning interrupt the moment the clock leaves its window, or escalate directly to a fault collector / destructive reset - no software polling needed.

The MEASURE mode is also useful at start-up: the application can measure the actual frequency of an internal RC oscillator (e.g. FIRC) once and then trim the system clock or recompute peripheral baud-rate dividers accordingly, getting tighter precision than the silicon's untrimmed tolerance.

### Functions implemented in device driver API
1. `clock_monitor_configure()` - install mode (WINDOW/MEASURE), per-mode parameters and an optional callback in one atomic call.
2. `clock_monitor_start()` - begin operation of the configured mode: continuous threshold checking (WINDOW) or one measurement (MEASURE) whose result is delivered through the configure-time callback
3. `clock_monitor_stop()` -stop frequency checking, or abort an in-flight measurement.
4. `clock_monitor_get_rate()` - poll the most recent completed measurement (0 / -EAGAIN in flight / -EIO clock lost / -ENOSYS no measurement hardware);.
5. `clock_monitor_set_source()` - Switch the reference / target clock inputs at runtime.

### Hardware references
1. NXP MCXE31 CMU_FC / CMU_FM (this PR ships back-ends for both)
2. NXP LPC55Sxx / i.MX RT5xx FREQME (MEASURE-only)
3. TI Hercules TMS570 / RM57 / AM26xx DCC (Dual Clock Comparator, WINDOW-only)
4. Renesas RA / RX CAC (WINDOW + MEASURE in one peripheral)
5. Infineon AURIX TC3xx CCU + SMU (WINDOW with safety-management escalation)
7. Infineon PSoC 6 / Traveo II CLK_MEAS_COUNTERS (MEASURE-only)
8. STMicroelectronics STM32 family CSS (LOST_ONLY)
10. Microchip PIC / dsPIC / SAM FSCM (LOST_ONLY)

title: modem: cellular: Allow defining separate script for DLC1 setup and PPP
body:
This is a follow up change for https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/107715

* Add separate state RUN_DLC1_SCRIPT before running the PPP dial script.
   Wait for network connection in this state, before issuing dial up command.
* Add new macro `MODEM_CELLULAR_NET_SCRIPT_DEFINE_INSTANCE()` for defining modem
  with DLC1 setup script.

These changes allow modem to be defined with a separate script
that runs on DLC1 channel and configures URC messages and joins the
network. This might be needed for some modems that do not accept `ATD*` or similar dial up commands before network is attached properly.

The PPP dial command can then be refactored to be only a single `ATD*99#`
or `AT+CGDATA` and it runs on DLC2.


Refactor BG95/BG96 driver to use DLC1 script to join the network and monifor `+CEREG` on the DLC1.
This is now possible as we don't do channel switches after https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/107715 so I can set up a static URC channel using `AT+QCFG="cmux/urcport",1`, so all URC messages come into DLC1.

Refactor nRF91 Serial Modem driver to use DLC1 script for joining and PPP setup.
The original design of `AT#XPPP=1` command in nRF91 means that PPP starts automatically when PDN is attached. This is now much more robust, as we don't do any channel switches, so the DLC1 stays as the "AT channel".
The change should also fix various recovery issues on Serial Modem 1.0 and later which are caused by the DLC1<-->DLC2 switch.

title: toolchain: iar: suppress Go004 via ALWAYS_INLINE override
body:
IAR emits diagnostic Go004 ("function cannot be inlined") for
every ALWAYS_INLINE function when optimisation is disabled, e.g.
in debug builds.  The previous workaround wrapped each affected
function in per-function preprocessor guard pairs:

  #ifdef IAR_SUPPRESS_ALWAYS_INLINE_WARNING_FLAG
  TOOLCHAIN_DISABLE_WARNING(TOOLCHAIN_WARNING_ALWAYS_INLINE)
  #endif
  static ALWAYS_INLINE void foo(...) { ... }
  #ifdef IAR_SUPPRESS_ALWAYS_INLINE_WARNING_FLAG
  TOOLCHAIN_ENABLE_WARNING(TOOLCHAIN_WARNING_ALWAYS_INLINE)
  #endif

This pattern is highly intrusive, scatters toolchain-specific
knowledge across generic source files, and requires a guard pair
every time a new ALWAYS_INLINE function is added for IAR.

Replace it with a single override of ALWAYS_INLINE inside
iccarm.h, using the C99 _Pragma operator to embed the diagnostic
suppression in the macro itself.

Introduce sys_regmap. It provides a strict C preprocessor symbol format for describing register address and bitfields within the registers, and provides C macros for generating and extracting fields from the register definitions.

The addition is primarily driven by me not wanting to manually copy register maps from datasheets to some ad-hoc defines in drivers, so I'm adding some nice macros along with very LLM friendly documentation so an LLM can generate the headers from any sort-of structured format, even OCR (visually reading documents).

Running gemma4 locally and giving it just the docs (without the "example output" part) it actually produces expected output
```                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
#define FOO_ADDR 0x39
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_OFFSET 0
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_SIZE 2
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_ENUM_DISABLED 0
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_ENUM_PUSH_PULL 1
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_ENUM_OPEN_DRAIN 2
#define FOO_FIELD_BAR_ENUM_OPEN_SOURCE 3
#define FOO_FIELD_BAZ_OFFSET 2
#define FOO_FIELD_BAZ_SIZE 1
#define FOO_FIELD_QUX_OFFSET 5
#define FOO_FIELD_QUX_SIZE 3
```

LMK what you think about this style of documentation, basically building in a prompt for generating appropriate code.

Some example uses:

	addr = SYS_REGMAP_GET_ADDR(REG_FEATURE_CTRL);
	value = SYS_REGMAP_GEN_FIELD_ENUM(REG_FEATURE_CTRL, ENGINE_EN, ENABLE);

	}

title: net: dns: validate rdata length in dns_unpack_answer
body:
dns_unpack_answer() validated only the fixed RR header size and accepted any rdlength, even one extending past the end of the packet. TXT and SRV consumers in resolve.c then read up to rdlength bytes from the message buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read on a truncated or crafted response.

Reject any RR whose declared rdata extends past dns_msg->msg_size at the single chokepoint in dns_unpack_answer(), so all current and future RR consumers are covered.

title: Allow DNS resolver to send queries to multiple servers
body:
### Summary

While looking over DNS resolver implementation, I have seen that a query is only sent to the first DNS server found in the server list. This might work, in some cases, but there are cases where there are multiple DNS servers present in a network and this scenario is not treated.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I was thinking to allow a query to be sent to all servers in the servers list.
This implies adding logic to track which server has been used for a pending query, how many responses have been received (if any, or multiple, if possible) and so on.
Right now, I am not sure which strategy would be suitable for this scenario. First response wins and all other queries to remaining servers are cancelled, or if a response aggregation might be required (I am not even sure at this moment if this is valid for DNS), or if resolver should wait for query timeout and then send the response.

title: net: sockets: fix TOCTOU in recvmsg/sendmsg
labels: area: Networking;area: Sockets;backport v3.7-branch;backport v4.3-branch;backport v4.4-branch
body:
z_vrfy_zsock_sendmsg() and z_vrfy_zsock_recvmsg() copy the user msghdr into msg_copy but then re-read msg->msg_iovlen (and other fields) live to size the allocation, bound the loop, and gate the writeback. A racing user thread can inflate msg_iovlen between reads, causing the verifier loop to write past the kernel iov shadow buffer.

Copy the msghdr first and use msg_copy for every later decision. Save the original user iov pointer and copy each iovec entry atomically so iov_base and iov_len cannot be raced apart.

Fixes: #112616

However, if the sensor was powered around the same time as the MCU, the soft reset itself may be sent too early, leading to the driver failing to initialize. Wait for the specified t_startup duration before sending the soft reset command.

title: bluetooth: classic: rfcomm: fix race condition in session disconnect
labels: area: Bluetooth;area: Bluetooth Classic;backport v3.7-branch;backport v4.3-branch;backport v4.4-branch
body:
Fix a race condition in RFCOMM session disconnection when both local and peer devices initiate disconnection simultaneously.

Add state check in `rfcomm_session_disconnected()` to only transition to `DISCONNECTED` state if the session is not already in `DISCONNECTING` state. This prevents the race condition where both sides set the session to disconnected, causing the disconnection process to not complete properly and leaving the L2CAP connection unreleased.

Without this check, subsequent RFCOMM channel connection requests would fail due to the invalid session state (the expected state is `IDLE`, while the actual state is `DISCONNECTED`).

Fixes: #110854

title: license_check: action_scancode and docker_scancode are incompatible with scancode-toolkit v32+
body:
### Describe the bug

The docker_scancode repository's main branch was updated to SCANCODE_RELEASE=32.5.0, but the ghcr.io/zephyrproject-rtos/scancode:v1.0.0 container image on GHCR was never rebuilt from it — that tag still contains the original ~4-year-old scancode v31.x binary. Because action_scancode's Dockerfile references FROM ghcr.io/zephyrproject-rtos/scancode:v1.0.0, and action_scancode's entrypoint.sh and license_check.py were also never updated for v32's breaking changes (the --license-policy flag now requires a file argument, and the per-file licenses JSON key was replaced by license_detections), the two repos are already incompatible with each other — but nobody has noticed because the stale v1.0.0 image masks the problem entirely. The moment that image is rebuilt or re-tagged from the current main branch Dockerfile, the Scan code for licenses CI job will fail for every Zephyr pull request.

### Regression

- [ ] This is a regression.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to the docker_scancode repository and note that the main branch Dockerfile sets SCANCODE_RELEASE=32.5.0.
2. Rebuild and push the ghcr.io/zephyrproject-rtos/scancode:v1.0.0 image from that main branch Dockerfile.
3. Open any Zephyr pull request that adds a new source file (to ensure the scan has files to process).
4. Observe the Scan code for licenses CI job fail at the scancode invocation step with: Error: Invalid value for '--license-policy': policy file is not a regular file — caused by entrypoint.sh passing --license-policy without a file argument, which is no longer valid in v32+.
5. Fix step 4 by removing --license-policy from entrypoint.sh, then re-run.
6. Observe the job now fail at the license_check.py step with: KeyError: 'licenses' — caused by license_check.py accessing file['licenses'], a key that was removed in scancode v32 and replaced with file['license_detections'].

```shell

```

### Impact

Functional Limitation – Some features not working as expected, but system usable.

### Environment

GitHub pull request ci

title: Bluetooth: Host: Always report completed ACL packets to controller
body:
## Problem

`bt_hci_host_num_completed_packets()` destroys the ACL RX buffer
unconditionally and is supposed to follow up with a
`HCI_Host_Number_Of_Completed_Packets` command so the controller can
keep its view of host buffer credits in sync. The function has two
early returns that skip this report:

1. `bt_conn_lookup_index(index)` returns `NULL` (the connection has
   already been torn down by the time we destroy the buffer).
2. The connection is in a state other than `BT_CONN_CONNECTED` or
   `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING`.

Each time we take either path, the ACL RX buffer is destroyed locally
without the controller learning that the credit is free again. After
`BT_BUF_HCI_ACL_RX_COUNT` such events, the controller believes the
host has zero free ACL RX buffers and stops sending any ACL data,
effectively wedging the link until the connection is re-established
or the controller is reset.

This is most easily observable on a host with a small
`BT_BUF_HCI_ACL_RX_COUNT` (i.e. small `CONFIG_BT_BUF_ACL_RX_COUNT_EXTRA`)
and a workload that triggers occasional late teardowns: the
"`Unable to look up conn with index ...`" warning fires
`BT_BUF_HCI_ACL_RX_COUNT` times and ACL RX traffic stops shortly
after.

## Fix

The state checks were defensive logging rather than load-bearing
correctness: the report message only needs the handle and count, and
both are read out of the buffer's `acl()` metadata before
`net_buf_destroy()` is called. There is no controller protocol reason
to skip the report when the conn pointer is missing or in an unusual
state.

Restructure to log warnings (still useful for diagnosing teardown
races) but always fall through to send the
`HCI_Host_Number_Of_Completed_Packets` report.

title: fs: ext2: validate directory entry structure before traversal
labels: bug;priority: medium;area: File System;backport v3.7-branch;backport v4.3-branch;backport v4.4-branch
body:
ext2_fetch_direntry() trusted the on-disk de_rec_len and de_name_len, and the lookup and readdir paths advanced traversal by an unvalidated de_rec_len. A crafted ext2 image could trigger an out-of-bounds read past the directory block buffer or a zero-progress loop in any path that walks a directory.

Validate rec_len and name_len in the parser, and reject entries whose header does not fit in the remaining block or whose rec_len would cross the block boundary in each caller.

labels: area: Samples;platform: STM32;area: Devicetree Binding;area: Audio;area: Boards/SoCs
body:
This PR aims to add support for DFSDM IP.  It provides support for STM32F7xx series, but the IP is available on F4/F7/H7/L4/L5/MP1/MP13 STM32 series.

### How it has been tested
On STM32F769I-Disco, the WM8994 codec is not yet supported, which does not allow to implement a loopback audio demo.
One way to test is to use the commit 2c97241e5d299bbecbc1bbae24714cf410b73b52 and break after the `dmic_read` loop (at line 78).  It is then possible to dump the raw buffer and decode it on the host computer using FFMpeg.

Here is a example dump that I recorded, and can be read with the following options:
`ffplay -f s16le -ar 16000 dump.bin.debug`
[dump.bin.debug](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27252350/dump.bin.debug)

### Caveats
* This driver only support IRQ mode, DMA mode will be provided later.
* It only supports regular conversion, which allows only one channel per filter.  Injected conversion will be provided later. This means that only mono recording can be done for one PDM (sync between 2 PDM can be achieved).
* ISR functions are statically implemented, while there can be max 4 filters (1 ISR per filter) here only one is used (which leads to unused function warning).
* Channel notion differs between STM32 documentation and Zephyr implementation.  This needs to be discussed.

Feel free to comment on this PR. I'll be glad to answer the best I can and provide enhancements.

### Next steps for this driver
* Support other STM32 series
* Support DMA
* Support injected conversions

### NB
The patch 2c97241e5d299bbecbc1bbae24714cf410b73b52 is not to be merged since it is only used for testing purpose.

title: drivers: i3c: cdns: calculate transfer timeout from message length
body:
Replace the fixed 1-second transfer timeout with a value derived from the actual number of SCL cycles required for the transfer, plus a configurable margin (I3C_CADENCE_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_US, default 10000 us).

Three helpers cover each transfer type:
- cdns_i3c_calc_timeout_i3c: SDR (broadcast header + 9 bits/byte) and HDR-DDR (ENTHDR0 preamble + DDR word count at 8 SCL cycles/word, including command header and CRC words)
- cdns_i3c_calc_timeout_i2c: 7-bit (9 bits) or 10-bit (18 bits) address frame + 9 bits per data byte, using the I2C SCL frequency
- cdns_i3c_calc_timeout_ccc: broadcast addr + CCC command byte + optional broadcast data + per-target address and data

title: MCUX EDMA breaks with I2S and networking enabled since SDK bump to 1.0
body:
### Describe the bug

When running the I2S output sample with `CONFIG_NETWORKING=y`, the EDMA cannot output the I2S samples. This behaviour was observed on the MIMXRT1064_EVK board, and can probably be extended to other boards using the nxp mcux edma.

Using git bisect, the issue seems to be introduced in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/d204d2487697b1db7a6e67ed961f522162c80324  (cmake: Set minimum required Zephyr SDK version to 1.0)

### Regression

- [x] This is a regression.

### Steps to reproduce

Using the mimxrt1062 QSPI board supported in the I2S output sample:

1. git checkout d204d2487697b1db7a6e67ed961f522162c80324
2. west update
3. west build -p -b mimxrt1060_evk/mimxrt1062/qspi samples/drivers/i2s/output/ -- -DCONFIG_NETWORKING=y
4. west flash

Running the exact same procedure on the parent commit (fc6753a60c32bfb1b122d5966ff90a9b42dcb24d) shows no issues


### Relevant log output

```shell
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v4.3.0-8452-gd204d2487697 ***
Could not write TX buffer 10
```

### Impact

Functional Limitation – Some features not working as expected, but system usable.

### Environment

- OS: WSL (Ubuntu)
- Toolchain: 1.0.0
- Commit SHA: d204d2487697b1db7a6e67ed961f522162c80324

### Additional Context

#### Additional logs
When taking the changes of https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/adb19db6c116cda1a14943053248e5de4dd354c1 into account, an error log is printed as well:
```
...
*** Booting Zephyr OS build v4.4.0-rc1-18-g94722df194ce ***
[00:00:00.013,000] <err> dma_mcux_edma: channel 0 error status is 0x80000004
...
```

#### Claude diagnosis
Running a diagnosis with Claude reveals the following:

**Why it broke with the SDK bump**: Zephyr SDK 1.0 ships with **binutils 2.43** (vs. 2.39 in SDK 0.16). Binutils 2.43 changed `SUBALIGN(n)` to be strict — it now forces each input section to exactly n-byte alignment, **overriding the section's declared alignment**. Old binutils would respect `max(SUBALIGN_n, section_alignment)`, so a section with `__aligned(32)` would still land at a 32-byte boundary even with `SUBALIGN(4)`. New binutils places it at only a 4-byte boundary.

**Why only with networking**: Without networking, `dtcm_bss` is empty, so `dtcm_noinit` starts at `0x20000000` — coincidentally 32-byte aligned, so even with strict `SUBALIGN(4)` the TCD pool is fine. With networking (PTP disabled since it's an audio sample), `dtcm_bss` gets 7 non-enhanced ENET descriptors × 8 bytes = **56 bytes**. `dtcm_noinit` then starts at `0x20000038` (56 is not a multiple of 32), the TCD pool lands at a non-32-byte-aligned address, and the new eDMA hardware immediately triggers SGE.

The fix is in the Zephyr linker script: change `SUBALIGN(4)` to `SUBALIGN(32)` on the `dtcm_noinit` section so each input section within it is guaranteed 32-byte alignment:

title: tests: drivers: dma: chan_blen_transfer: use literal ZTEST names
body:
The chan_blen_transfer test generated its ZTEST cases through a FOR_EACH(TEST_TASK, (), DMA_LIST) wrapper that token-pasted the DMA node label into the test name, e.g.:

    ZTEST(dma_m2m, test_##dma_name##_m2m_chan0_burst8)

At runtime the C preprocessor expands these correctly and ztest reports the real names (test_tst_dma0_m2m_chan0_burst8, etc.), so the suite passes on the device. However, twister's static source parser in scripts/pylib/twister does not run the preprocessor when scanning for ZTEST(suite, name) literals to build the expected-testcase list. With an unresolved `dma_name` token, it registers a phantom testcase with an empty trailing name:

    drivers.dma.chan_blen_transfer.dma_m2m.

That phantom case never receives a result and is reported with status=None, polluting CI dashboards and forcing a quarantine entry across every platform that runs the suite (CY8CKIT_041S_MAX, KIT_PSC3M5_EVK, KIT_PSE84_AI m33/m55, KIT_PSE84_EVAL m33/m55).

Fix this by writing the ZTEST() invocations with literal test names that match what ztest emits at runtime. The shared body is factored into a small RUN_DMA_M2M_TEST() helper to keep the cases compact, and the tst_dma1 cases are gated on CONFIG_DMA_LOOP_TRANSFER_NUMBER_OF_DMAS to preserve multi-controller support. A #error guards future bumps beyond two DMA controllers so the test is updated explicitly rather than silently losing coverage.

No functional/runtime change - the same test bodies execute with the same names; only the static discovery path is fixed so twister's expected list aligns with the reported results.
